find: if (!tally) return unknown("the journal tally is unreadable");
replace: if (!tally) return pass("the journal tally is unreadable");
why: a tally the probe cannot read must be unknown, never a pass that closes an open issue
the tally prints at most five sessions, so a window of six judges no bot and every silent bot reads quiet
a bot whose newest live session is this week must be judged; only a bot idle for over ten days is skipped

find:
if (!outside) return quiet("judged after the close, so the read never slows a trading cycle");
      if (outside.status === "unknown") return outside;
why: the probe must not run the tally while the regular session is open: a trading cycle on a one-CPU machine never waits on a multi-megabyte read
the journal is read on the primary machine; the first machine Fly lists may be a standby with an empty or stale volume
the read on the machine is the plain tally command with no shell; the exec arguments are the contract with the machine
a scout picking or closing is not a bot deciding, so its journal must never appear in the tally as a bot
only a record with mode live counts; a bot held to watching proposes and places nothing by design and must not be judged
a reason is a broker rejection or a cooldown skip; an outcome with any other action is not an explanation and must not excuse a silent bot
sessions are New York days; a record after 8 pm New York belongs to that day, and under UTC it starts a day that never traded
archives are read newest first so the stop rule lands on the five newest days; oldest first fills the window with stale days and stops before the recent silent ones
reading stops only once a sixth day proves the fifth is whole; stopping at five drops the half of the fifth day that sits in the next older file, including its placed order or refusal
